**Continuous 2.16.2**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.16.2.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.16.2.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.16.2.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.16.2.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.16.2.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.16.2.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.16.2.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.16.2-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.16.2.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.16.2-vscode/continuous-cli-2.16.2.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.16.1

A hotfix release. A reply stopped while the model was still reasoning (for example by an accidental Ctrl+Backspace) could break every later request, and on Bedrock it failed with "no content in assistant message before conversational turn change". This release fixes that at both ends, removes the Ctrl+Backspace shortcut that stopped replies by accident, and adds Resume for a stopped or failed response.

### Behaviour changes

- **Ctrl+Backspace no longer cancels anything.** Ctrl+Backspace (Cmd+Backspace on macOS, Alt+Backspace in JetBrains) used to stop the running response and reject a pending tool call, even when you were only deleting a word in the chat input, and work was lost that way. Backspace with any of those modifiers now only edits text, while a response is streaming too. Stop a response or a running terminal command with the **Stop** button, and reject a command with its **Reject** button. The `Shift+Ctrl+Backspace` (`Shift+Cmd+Backspace`) shortcut that rejects all diff changes in VS Code is unchanged.

### Fixes

- **Stopping a reply while the model is still reasoning no longer breaks the next request.** Stop, or a request that failed, used to keep the model's reasoning as if it were an answer, so the next message sent a reply holding only reasoning; Bedrock refused it ("no content in assistant message before conversational turn change") and other providers could reject it too. The reasoning stays on screen but is no longer sent, a partial answer is kept as before, and a tool call that was still being written is cancelled. Saved sessions that already hold such a reply are sent correctly too.

- Bedrock no longer fails with "no content in assistant message before conversational turn change". A turn that converts to nothing (a reply stopped or failed before any text, reasoning a non-Claude model can't take back, a tool call without an id, a user message whose context or image rendered empty) is now left out and the turns around it are joined, so the request keeps the alternating roles Converse requires. The CLI, which sent two messages of the same role in that case, gets the same repair. A history that was already valid is sent byte for byte as before, so prompt caching is unaffected.

### New

- **Resume a stopped or failed response.** When you stop a reply, a request fails, or the window closes or reloads while the agent works, the chat shows **Resume** under the last turn (a keyboard-reachable button named "Resume response"), including when you reopen that session from history. Resume carries on without retyping: a partial answer is kept and the model is asked to continue from it, and a turn that had no answer yet sends your message again in its place. Tool calls that already ran keep their results and are not run again; a tool call stopped before it ran is not run either, and the model is told so, so if it still needs it, it asks again and the current mode decides whether that needs your approval. In the CLI, pressing Enter on an empty prompt after an interrupt already resumes.
